title: Would You Call vs Phil Ivey?

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: [excited] Welcome to the Shark Cage! A million dollars on the line... and across the table sits the most feared man in poker. [dramatic] Phil. Ivey.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: [nervous] Okay. Deep breath. It's just a card game. Against... the final boss.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: [delighted] Ace-queen. Suited. Ooh, that's pretty.

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: Ivey raises from under the gun. Thirty-eight thousand.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: [confident] Ace-queen suited, on the button? I'm not folding this. Call.

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: [excited] The flop! Eight... eight... ACE!

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: [smug] Aces up! Two pair, queen kicker. I'm basically a genius.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: He checks. Let's bet fifty thousand.

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: And Ivey... calls. No emotion. None. [whispers] Is he even breathing?

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: The turn. A seven.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: He checks again. I'll check too. Pot control. [proud] Very professional.

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: The river... a nine. And Ivey checks. For the third time.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: [confident] Three checks. He's weak. He HAS to be weak. A hundred and twenty-five thousand.

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: [slowly, dramatic] And Phil Ivey... check-raises... to FOUR HUNDRED AND FIFTY THOUSAND!

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: [panicking] Wait. What. WHY. He checked three times! Okay, think. What beats me? Aces... ace-eight... any eight... jack-ten...

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: [nervous] I've come this far. I... call.

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: [shouting] ACES! Phil Ivey has ACES FULL! He trapped her the ENTIRE hand!

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: [deadpan] Cool. Cool cool cool.

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: The lesson? Ace-queen is a great hand. But against a player like Ivey, you're not getting three streets of value. And when he check-raises the river... [serious] he usually has it.

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: [excited] Would YOU have called? Tell me in the comments. And subscribe... or Ivey will check-raise you too.

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: [intense] Would YOU call?

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: [calm, explaining] Quick lesson. Ace-queen suited is one of the ten best starting hands. Against an early raise, calling on the button is great. A three-bet is fine too.

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: [calm, explaining] On an eight, eight, ace flop, you have aces up. That's a strong hand, so betting for value is right.

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: [calm, explaining] Checking the turn keeps the pot small, and gives Ivey a chance to bluff.

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: [calm, explaining] Be careful though. Three checks don't always mean weak. Great players check their monsters to set a trap.

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: [calm, explaining] So what beats you here? Aces. Ace-eight. Any eight. Nines or sevens full. Ace-king. Jack-ten. Ten-six. And a river check-raise from Ivey is usually one of those.

lines.speaker: caster
lines.text: [calm, explaining] Now the math. You have to call three hundred twenty-five thousand to win one point one million. So you need to be right about thirty percent of the time.
